correctness.rationale: The cubic interpolation weights were independently differentiated and checked for polynomial exactness through degree 3. Their difference recurrence yields explicit A(r), B(r), whose two-period trace/determinant are verified by symbolic multiplication. The three factored Jury inequalities after scaling eigenvalues by 5 have strictly positive coefficients for every r>0. Trace and determinant limits yield the sharp supremum 1/5; fixed-ratio decay makes differences summable, and the explicit initial-data construction shows ratio-dependent transients. The packaged verifier replayed 116 symbolic and exact-rational checks. This is an infinite analytic proof, not an inference from numerical samples.

value.rationale: BDF3 ratio restrictions are central to adaptive numerical time stepping. A complete infinite class of arbitrarily unequal but repeated two-period grids is shown to have a sharp uniformly small parasitic Floquet spectral radius, beyond the range of published general-grid sufficient bounds. The example separating that bound from arbitrarily large starting-error transients is necessary for principled interpretation. The result is a usable stability benchmark, not a routine restatement of classical root criteria or an arbitrary finite parameter example.
